To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the energy-efficient reference understeer gradient of a four-wheel-drive electric torque-vectoring vehicle is a decreasing function of the lateral acceleration”.

1) the understeer characteristics of a torque-vectoring vehicle should not be designed to maximize the vehicle lateral acceleration; 2) it is better to significantly reduce the understeering behavior of the vehicle, in particular at low speeds, to improve its energy efficiency.

1) the reference vehicle understeering characteristic can be designed in a way to maximize the vehicle efficiency, and 2) the most efficient understeering characteristic is characterized by a significantly reduced level of understeer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and experimental validation of a novel understeer characteristic for torque-vectoring four-wheel-drive fully electric vehicles.
the novel experimentally based design of a vehicle understeer reference characteristic that provides energy efficiency enhancement.
the development of a reference vehicle handling quality characteristic for energy-efficient electric vehicles with multiple electric motors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, to maximize the energy efficiency, it is better to reduce the under/oversteer level of the vehicle with respect to the reference vehicle without torque-vectorization.
the torque-vectoring control strategy can be designed to achieve energy efficiency improvements, while keeping the vehicle handling quality at a high level.
the torque-vectoring control of the electric vehicle demonstrator can be used to achieve both improved energy efficiency and vehicle handling quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the design of the understeer characteristic is an important factor for energy-efficient vehicle handling, and it can be tuned to provide energy efficiency improvements with respect to a vehicle with the same handling qualities, but with even torque distribution at the wheels.
a more efficient torque-vectoring control strategy can be designed by considering energy efficiency as a design target.
, for the case study, it is more energy efficient to have a more oversteery behavior during cornering, and this is true over the whole range achievable of lateral accelerations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

energy efficiency and handling performance are not conflicting requirements, and that it is possible to design the reference understeering characteristic of the vehicle to improve energy efficiency while keeping the vehicle handling quality at an acceptable level.
energy-efficient torque-vectoring control is not only possible but it can be designed to provide the same level of vehicle handling as the same vehicle without any torque-vectoring control.

, in the case of a fully electric vehicle with torque-vectoring, it is possible not only to increase the maximum lateral accelerations and the level of vehicle stability but also to improve the vehicle energy efficiency.
